name: vivarium-near-boulders-day-a
refs: IMAGE 1, THE AUTHORITY (room 1's signed close-up by day): the camera at ground level, the lens, the depth of field, the scale, the finish and the light. Never the layout of its planting; none of its floor dressing (roots, succulents, stones, seep) appears:
IMAGE 2, THE LAYOUT MAP (structure and placement only, never the look), a diagram; nothing of it is painted: the dark grey above is the soft back; the light grey below is the ground:
IMAGE 3, SUBJECT AND MATERIAL ONLY (sandstone stone and scree): never its flat, toon-like finish, never its angular flat-topped slabs:
prompt: Output a NEW image, 4:3: this room seen much CLOSER and at GROUND LEVEL, at the creatures' scale, in the same warm daylight from the upper left, the same Miniature Lives finish (fine grain, soft bokeh behind) as Image 1. THE NEW PICTURE: the rounded flank of a sandstone boulder filling the left side (the left quarter of the width); a slope of fine scree and cushion plants at the right; the floor across the centre open and finely pebbled. The open floor across the centre of the lower part (from about 25 to 75 percent of the width and from about 72 to 86 percent of the height, inside the light grey of Image 2) is moss or soil only, sunlit as brightly as Image 1's floor, nothing on it taller than a tiny pebble; nothing busy directly behind the middle of the picture: the features frame it from the sides and from far back. No creatures, no animals, no figures, no text, no letters, no digits, no frame, no UI, no pool, no open water, no cliff or ledge. Cute by craft, never childish: no cartoon outlines, no toy colours, no gloss, no glow.
